notes.summary: Reconstructed new102: locally bounded generated CLD Psh sections have middle-positive doubly closed ordinary multipliers through every sheafified ordinal, for all original fields and current degrees. This establishes separate-product positivity, not P21.3 equality.
notes.detailedSummary: The locally bounded final section forces every decreasing predecessor to be finite and locally bounded. A direct coefficient-matrix argument justifies Borel multiplication for middle-positive currents without strongly-positive spanning. Bounded convergence against fixed compact coefficient measures handles successors; ordinary locality handles intermediate sheafification and limit ranks. The theorem includes trivial valuation, singularities, nilpotents and continuous generated-Psh potentials without reverse CPsh recognition. Equal canonical curvatures still do not provide a two-sign generating construction for the difference. No universal equality or analytic counterexample was obtained.
notes.text:
Original P21.3 remains unresolved; candidate=false. The following is an unverified proof reconstruction of the supplied new102 suggestion.

Theorem. Let K be any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation; X good, separated, strict, boundaryless and pure of dimension n>=2; W any ordinary open. Let T be a middle-positive ordinary CLD (p,p) current, 0<=p<=n-1, with d'T=d''T=0. For every locally bounded real section f of generated CLD Psh(W), its ordinary Borel product fT exists and D(fT), D=d'd'', is middle-positive and doubly closed. No reduction or change of generic multiplicities is made.

Exact external premises. CLD means arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2. Definition 8.1.1 generates the minimal ordinary sheaf from smooth positive-Hessian functions and decreasing sequential limits; 8.1.4 supplies ordinary-local successor limits and earlier-rank membership at limits. Proposition 6.5.2 decomposes compact symmetric tests into two compact middle-positive tests; its analytic support scope includes almost-good spaces, hence the present good spaces. Sections 7.2.1–4 give middle positivity and locality; 7.2.7(b) gives positive smooth-factor multiplication. Sections 7.2.8 and 7.2.11 supply positive scalar coefficient Radon measures. Sections 1.2.6–7 identify middle positivity with signed positive-semidefinite coefficient matrices on exterior powers; 7.1.1–3 supply chartwise current-continuity criteria. Only compact moment-image polyhedrality from 12.2.4 is used, not its printed dimension-equality clause. Ordinary restriction, smooth multiplication and differential identities are 7.1.6–7, 8.5.3–4 and 7.7.1–5. Their applicability to the present ordinary opens follows from 11.1.7, 15.2.2–9 and 15.7.1–2. Canonical integration retains generic lengths by 16.6.3. These published statements are external premises; reverse CPsh recognition is not assumed.

Borel product audit. For a compact symmetric complementary test eta, write eta=eta1-eta2 with compact middle-positive tests and define mu_eta=mu_eta1-mu_eta2 using T's coefficient measures. Different decompositions agree on compact smooth scalars, hence by smooth density on compact continuous scalars, hence as Radon measures. This proves independence and linearity. The signed measure is supported in supp eta, since its functional vanishes on scalars supported in the complementary open. Define <fT,eta>=integral f dmu_eta; discard the antisymmetric test part by symmetry.

This functional is an ordinary order-zero current even for discontinuous locally bounded Borel f. Localize a fixed test family to a moment g:O->E using a compact nonnegative smooth scalar rho. Choose a compact analytic domain C inside O with supp rho in its interior. The moment image P has finitely many tangent faces. For Euclidean coordinates set Theta=sum d'x_i wedge d''x_i. On each tangent face of dimension at least q, Theta^q has a positive-definite signed coefficient matrix on its qth exterior power. Finite-dimensional matrix domination, with the maximum constant over the finitely many faces, gives
  c||a||_(P,0)Theta^q +/- a >=0
for every symmetric presented (q,q) test a. Lower-dimensional faces give zero restrictions; q=0 uses Theta^0=1. Pullback and multiplication by rho preserve middle positivity. Consequently
  |mu_(rho g*a)| <= c||a||_(P,0)mu_(rho g*Theta^q),
and therefore
  |<fT,rho g*a>| <= c||f||_(supp rho)||a||_(P,0)<T,rho g*Theta^q>.
This fixed C^0 bound and finite smooth localization prove current continuity. Smooth multiplication agrees with the original calculus. Restriction follows by extending compact tests by zero and identifying coefficient measures. The argument uses the middle cone, not strongly-positive spanning.

Ordinal proof. Define P_0 by smooth positive Hessians; P_(xi+1) by ordinary-local decreasing sequences from P_xi; P_lambda by ordinary-local earlier-stage membership. Every stage is upper semicontinuous: decreasing infima satisfy {inf_j f_j<a}=union_j{f_j<a}, and upper semicontinuity is local at limits. Finite sections are Borel. The stages increase and stabilize because the collection of all ordinary-open/ambient-section pairs is a set. A stationary stage is a sheaf containing the generators and closed under decreasing sequences on every fixed open. Minimality identifies it with generated Psh; no integrability qualification is added to the definition.

Induct simultaneously over every ordinary open and allowed current. At rank zero, both closedness equations give D(fT)=Df wedge T, which is middle-positive. At a successor, on an ordinary neighbourhood N write f_j in P_xi(N), decreasing to the locally bounded real final f. Since f_j>=f, each predecessor is finite: -infinity is impossible, and +infinity is excluded by the function sheaf. The final f supplies local lower bounds; finite upper semicontinuity of each f_j supplies local upper bounds. Thus each predecessor is locally bounded, so induction applies without asserting continuity or a global smooth presentation.

Fix a compact symmetric smooth test alpha of degree (n-p-1,n-p-1). Decompose Dalpha=eta1-eta2 into compact middle-positive tests. Their coefficient measures mu1,mu2 belong to the fixed T|N and are finite. On their compact support union C there are finite bounds, independent of j,
  a<=f<=f_j<=f_1<=b.
For g_j=f_j-f, the Borel sets E_j={g_j>=epsilon} decrease to empty. Countable additivity and finiteness imply mu_i(E_j)->0, and
  integral g_j dmu_i <= epsilon mu_i(C)+(b-a)mu_i(E_j).
Letting j tend to infinity and then epsilon to zero proves
  <D(f_jT),alpha> -> <D(fT),alpha>.
For positive alpha the left side is nonnegative by induction. Symmetry of fT and DJ=JD give symmetry of the Hessian. Ordinary restriction and positivity locality conclude on W. Intermediate predecessor covers are handled by the preceding inductive theorem; no potentials are glued. At a limit rank, locally bounded f belongs near each point to one earlier stage, so induction and locality conclude. No common global earlier rank or infinite intersection of neighbourhoods is needed. Stabilization finishes the proof. Finally d'DS=0 and d''DS=-d'(d'')^2S=0 for every current S. The scalar-test endpoint p=n-1 is included.

Consequences and limitation. Iteration defines an ORDERED positive doubly closed recursion T_0=T, T_k=D(f_kT_(k-1)) for locally bounded generated-Psh f_k and k<=n-p. Neither commutativity nor curvature-independence is proved. If both h and -h belong to generated Psh, positivity of both signs of D(hT), symmetric-test decomposition and symmetry imply D(hT)=0. For the original h=U-V, equal canonical Hessians have not supplied these two memberships. Separate decreasing representations also supply no predecessor curvature relation to pass to their limits. Thus positivity of D(UT) and D(VT) does not establish their equality.

notes.summary: Affinoid analytic diagnostic: every linear subspace of classical pluriharmonic functions on a fixed compact affinoid is closed under pointwise convergent nets, with uniform convergence. This provides no recognition of an arbitrary P21.3 difference or multiplier equality.
notes.detailedSummary: GR Shilov evaluation embeds the classical pluriharmonic space into a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and determines its supremum norm. Closedness of every linear evaluation subspace proves the net assertion without assuming continuity of the finite pointwise limit. Consequently nets of ordinary smooth classical harmonic functions on one fixed compact affinoid cannot produce nonsmooth limits. GR real-PL recognition still requires already classical pluriharmonic input and an actual strictly semistable model over a nontrivially valued field. None of these missing hypotheses is established for arbitrary original pair differences.
notes.text:
Theorem. Let A be a compact K-affinoid space over any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation. Let PH(A) denote CLASSICAL pluriharmonic functions and L any real linear subspace of PH(A). If a net h_a in L converges pointwise on A to a finite real function h, then h belongs to L and convergence is uniform. Continuity of h is a conclusion, not a hypothesis. The same assertion holds on a compact analytic space with a finite affinoid-domain cover.

Exact primary premise. GR means Gubler–Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2. Definition 7.1 requires both signs to be classically psh; 7.2 gives continuity and a real vector space. Proposition 7.3 states that on an affinoid with finite Shilov boundary Gamma, already classical pluriharmonic functions attain their maximum and minimum on Gamma, and evaluation PH(A)->R^Gamma is injective. The field convention permits trivial valuation; 7.3 adds no strictness, smoothness or reducedness assumption. This published analytic theorem is an external premise, not an independently audited proof of all its foundations. The relevant literal statements and printed proofs, including the supporting maximum-principle proof 6.4, were read through the public primary PDF browser and preserved under premise index 7. Only browser-text hashes are claimed; original GR PDF bytes were unavailable.

Proof. Evaluation E:PH(A)->R^Gamma is a linear injection. The maximum/minimum assertion gives ||v||_A=max_Gamma|v| for every v in PH(A). The image E(L) is a linear subspace of finite-dimensional R^Gamma and is closed: extend a basis to a full basis and express the subspace as the common zero set of the remaining coordinate functionals. Pointwise convergence of the original directed net on finite Gamma is Euclidean convergence, since a common upper index handles its finitely many coordinates for each tolerance. Its limit therefore equals E(v) for some v in L. Applying the norm identity to h_a-v yields uniform convergence to v. Uniqueness of pointwise limits gives h=v. No replacement of the net by a sequence is made. For a finite affinoid-domain cover, use the union of the Shilov boundaries; its finite evaluations likewise determine the global supremum norm.

Approximation consequence. The functions in PH(A) that are ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth FORM Hessian form a linear subspace. Every pointwise net limit of them on this SAME A is already in that subspace. In the good strict CLD scope, such smooth functions have both signs among the generated Psh generators, and GR section 1.2's published inclusion into classical psh places them in PH(A). Thus replacing sequences by nets on a fixed affinoid does not produce nonsmooth harmonic limits. This says nothing about shrinking approximation domains or recognition of arbitrary ordinary zero-current functions.

Research boundary. GR 1.2 recognizes U and V separately as classically psh but supplies no subtraction closure. The ambient equation D[U]=D[V] has not been shown to imply that both signs of U-V pass every classical curve test after every analytic field extension. GR 7.8 further requires a nontrivially valued field and an actual strictly semistable formal model of a good quasicompact strict domain. No such model or recognition theorem is obtained for arbitrary original germs. The net theorem gives no new Bedford–Taylor range and no analytic counterexample.

A concrete sufficient statement still unproved is a valid ordinary-local generating construction of BOTH U-V and V-U on one fixed neighbourhood for every actual continuous generated-Psh equal-curvature pair. Another route would need actual positive doubly closed current regularization compatible with all analytic refinements, or direct preservation of signed curvature relations. No ambient Hessian restriction to curves, transcendental scalar-current ascent, strong lift/product bridge or current-density theorem is assumed or proved. No admissible analytic pair, current and compact smooth test producing a nonzero product difference was constructed.
